image.alt: A Philodendron Paraiso Verde in a white pot, its long wavy leaves marbled in cream and pale green over deep green

light.label: Bright indirect light
light.note: Tolerates medium light, with slower growth and less marbling

landscape_use.note: Frost-free zones, out of direct sun

snap: A climbing Philodendron with long, slightly wavy leaves marbled in cream and pale green over deep green, no two alike. It wants bright filtered light and steadier humidity than most, and is toxic to cats and dogs if chewed.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: A cultivated plant whose parentage is still unsettled, usually placed near Philodendron giganteum. It climbs, and the leaves lengthen considerably once it has a pole to hold — a specimen left trailing never shows what it can do.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Water when the top inch of the mix has dried, in a loose aroid mix. Humidity matters more here than with most Philodendrons: dry air, and hard or chlorinated water, are the usual reasons new leaves come out with brown tips.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: The marbling is painted rather than blocked — cream and pale green running in streaks through deep green, so every leaf is different and new ones open almost white before they harden and green up.
